question: Who among the following was the first ruler who inscribed his message on stone surfaces for his subjects and officials?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Emperor Ashoka (304 - 232 BCE) was the third king of the Maurya Dynasty. Remorseful after his bloody campaign and conquest of Kalinga, Ashoka embraced Buddhism.
 
• Ashoka__:
 __
 
• Ashoka was the emperor of India's Maurya Dynasty from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• Ashoka is referred to as Buddhsakya in Maski Inscription and Dharmakosa in his Sarnath Inscription.
 
• He was known as Devampiya i.e. beloved of Goda, and as Piyadassi i.e. of pleasing appearance.
 
• Ashoka believed in the policy of Dhamma.
 
• Ashoka's visit to Lumbini and exemption of Lumbini from tax was mentioned in Rumminidei Pillar Inscription.
 
• The Kandhar Inscription speaks about the success of his policy with the hunters and fishermen.
 
• Nigalisagar Pillar Inscription: It mentions that Ashoka increased the height of the stupa of Buddha Konakamana to its double size.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• Chanakya was the teacher of Chandragupta Maurya__.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Maurya dynasty.
 
• He is credited with the setting up of the first pan-Indian empire.
 
• Chanakya, also called Kautilya or Vishnugupta played a key role in helping Chandragupta overthrow the powerful Nanda dynasty at Pataliputra, in the Magadha region.
 
• Artha-shastra, (“The Science of Material Gain”), written by Kautilya on statecraft, economic policy and military strategy came to be Chandragupta’s guide.
 
• The ideas expressed by Kautilya in the Arthashastra are totally practical and unsentimental.
 
 
 
• **Harshavardhan**
 
 
• HARSHAVARDHAN (606 CE – 647 CE)
 
• During Harshavardhana’s rule, Kannauj was conquered and united with Thaneswar.
 
• He attacked Shashank of Gauda Kingdom and established his control over regions of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha and befriended Bhashkarvarman of Kamrup (Assam).
 
• Vallabhi King Dhruvbhata in Gujrat too was defeated and a truce was negotiated with him by the marriage of Harsha’s daughter to Dhruvbhata.
 
• He assumed titles of Uttarapathanatha or Uttarapathapati (Lord of the North).
 
• While marching southwards, Harshavardhan conquered regions of Malawa and after crossing Narmada he was defeated by Pulkeshin II in the Battle of Narmada.
 
• He was greatly influenced by the personality of Hieun Tsang and organized a Buddhist assembly at Kannauj under his chairmanship.

• **​Chandragupta I**
 
 
• Chandragupta I married Kumara Devi who was a Lichchavi princess.
 
• The Lichchavi dynasty was a kingdom that existed in Nepal from 400 to 750 CE.
 
• Marrying the Lachchavi princess enabled Chandragupta I to expand his territory to Nepal.
